faqs.question: What is a WhatsApp broadcast?
faqs.answer: A WhatsApp broadcast is a way to send one message to many selected recipients while keeping each recipient's conversation private. In a business workflow, broadcasts should be sent only to people who have opted in and should use approved templates when required by the WhatsApp Business Platform.

faqs.question: Can I broadcast on WhatsApp without a CRM?
faqs.answer: Yes, very small teams can use the WhatsApp Business app broadcast-list feature. Larger teams usually need a CRM or WhatsApp Business Platform workflow for consent records, approved templates, segmentation, scheduling, failure handling, and reply ownership.

faqs.question: Do WhatsApp broadcasts need approved templates?
faqs.answer: If the business initiates a message outside the customer service window on the WhatsApp Business Platform, it normally needs an approved message template. App-only broadcast behavior is different, but teams should still avoid sending unwanted messages.

faqs.question: How do I avoid spam complaints when broadcasting on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Send only to opted-in contacts, keep the message relevant to the audience, identify the business clearly, give people an easy way to stop receiving messages, limit frequency, and monitor blocks, failures, and replies.

faqs.question: What should I track after sending a WhatsApp broadcast?
faqs.answer: Track queued, sent, delivered, failed, replied, opted out, and handoff states. Delivery alone is not enough because replies, failures, consent changes, and follow-up ownership determine whether the campaign was useful.

faqs.question: Where does TalkWagon fit in a WhatsApp broadcast workflow?
faqs.answer: TalkWagon helps teams prepare contact audiences, use approved templates, run broadcasts, track message progress, manage replies in the team inbox, and connect follow-up work to contacts, pipelines, automations, and human agents.
